slides.heading: FCC Approves Jamming Technology for Prisons
slides.text: The FCC voted to allow state and local prisons to use jamming technology to block contraband cellphones, despite concerns about blocking lawful communications.

slides.heading: Background
slides.text: The FCC approved the jamming order at its meeting yesterday. The technology has advanced to the point where it can be focused with geographic precision. No facility will be required to do it.

slides.heading: Impact
slides.text: The pilot test showed substantial gaps in jamming the targeted “contraband” devices, with testing scenarios in outdoor inmate recreation areas showing failure rates—meaning “contraband” device call completion—in one-half to two-thirds of call attempts.
